name: Hosting controller
first: A UIKit view controller that shows a SwiftUI view, so that a UIKit app can use SwiftUI one screen at a time.

dependsOn.why: A hosting controller shows a SwiftUI view, and runs its body as SwiftUI does in an app.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The type `Greeting` is a view with a `body`, as `Greeting` is on the page of View.

dependsOn.why: A UIKit view controller is a class, which UIKit code holds by reference.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The constant `host` holds a reference to the controller, as `first` holds a reference to a `Counter` on the page of Class.

what.is: A `UIHostingController` is a UIKit view controller that shows a SwiftUI view, its root view. A UIKit app uses it as any other view controller, such as by pushing it or presenting it, so the app can add SwiftUI one screen at a time.
what.afterExample: The hosting controller holds a `Greeting` as its root view. When it is asked what size it needs, it lays out the SwiftUI view, which runs its `body`. The program runs on an iPhone in the simulator, because UIKit is a framework of iOS.
what.problem: Many apps were written in UIKit, and cannot be written again all at once. A hosting controller lets a UIKit app show a new screen written in SwiftUI, beside its UIKit screens.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that a hosting controller manages a SwiftUI view hierarchy, that its root view is given when it is made and can be changed later through `rootView`, and that it is used like any other view controller. Its view draws the SwiftUI views, and SwiftUI updates them as it does in a SwiftUI app.

when.text: Use it to show SwiftUI in a UIKit app, such as a new settings screen pushed by a UIKit navigation controller.
Don't use it in an app that is all SwiftUI. There, views are already shown inside the app's scenes.

parts.name: The root view, line 12
parts.text: The argument `rootView` is the SwiftUI view that the controller shows: a `Greeting`. The property `rootView` reads it, and setting the property shows a different view.

Line 14 prints the type of its root view: {{Greeting}}.
Line 16 asks the controller what size it needs inside 300 by 300 points, the size on line 15. It lays out its SwiftUI view, so the `body` of `Greeting` runs, and line 6 prints {{body runs}}.
Line 17 prints whether the size is more than zero across and down: {{true true}}. It is the size of the text Trips.
